sentences.zh: 羅憲

translations.literal: Luo Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian.

sentences.zh: 羅憲，字令則，襄陽人也。

translations.literal: Luo Xian, courtesy name Lingze, was a man of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian, whose courtesy name was Lingze, came from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，蜀廣漢太守。

translations.literal: His father Luo Meng was Administrator of Guanghan in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Luo Meng, had served as Administrator of Guanghan in Shu.

sentences.zh: 憲年十三，能屬文，早知名。

translations.literal: At age thirteen Xian could compose literary essays and was early known by reputation.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he could already write polished prose and had begun to make a name for himself.

sentences.zh: 師事譙周，周門人稱為子貢。

translations.literal: He studied under Qiao Zhou, and Zhou's disciples called him Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Qiao Zhou, whose students nicknamed him Zigong after Confucius's disciple.

sentences.zh: 性方亮嚴整，待士無倦，輕財好施，不營產業。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, bright, strict, and orderly; he treated gentlemen tirelessly; he regarded wealth lightly and liked to give; he did not pursue estates.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright, principled, and disciplined; he treated scholars with inexhaustible courtesy; he cared little for money and gave freely, and he never bothered to build up landed property.

sentences.zh: 仕蜀為太子舍人、宣信校尉。

translations.literal: He served Shu as Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Colonel Who Makes Trust Manifest.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he served as a gentleman attendant to the heir apparent and as Colonel Who Makes Trust Manifest.

sentences.zh: 再使于吳，吳人稱焉。

translations.literal: Twice he was sent as envoy to Wu, and the people of Wu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent twice as envoy to Wu, he earned high praise there.

sentences.zh: 時黃皓預政，眾多附之，憲獨介然。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Hao interfered in government, and the multitude largely attached itself to him; Xian alone stood apart.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch Huang Hao dominated the court and most officials curried his favor, Xian alone held himself aloof.

sentences.zh: 皓恚之，左遷巴東太守。

translations.literal: Hao resented him and demoted him to be Administrator of Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao, furious at him, had him relegated to Administrator of Badong.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍閻宇都督巴東，拜憲領軍，為宇副貳。

translations.literal: At the time Grand General Yan Yu supervised Badong; Xian was appointed to command the army as Yan Yu's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yan Yu was overall commander in Badong; Xian was named army commander and served as his second.

sentences.zh: 魏之伐蜀，召宇西還，憲守永安城。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Shu, Yan Yu was summoned back west, and Xian defended Yong'an city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded Shu, Yan Yu was recalled westward, leaving Xian to hold Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 及成都敗，城中擾動，邊江長吏皆棄城走，憲斬亂者一人，百姓乃安。

translations.literal: When Chengdu fell, there was turmoil in the city; all the riverside officials along the border abandoned their cities and fled. Xian executed one who stirred disorder, and the common people then were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengdu fell the town was in uproar; magistrates along the river threw away their posts and ran. Xian executed one ringleader and the people settled down.

sentences.zh: 知劉禪降，乃率所統臨於都亭三日。

translations.literal: Learning that Liu Shan had surrendered, he then led those under his command to mourn at the metropolitan pavilion for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Liu Shan had surrendered, he led his troops to the roadside pavilion and mourned there for three days.

sentences.zh: 吳聞蜀敗，遣將軍盛憲西上，外托救援，內欲襲憲。

translations.literal: Wu heard that Shu had been defeated and sent General Sheng Xian westward; outwardly claiming relief, inwardly intending to attack Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu heard of Shu's collapse it sent General Sheng Xian upriver from the east—ostensibly to help, in truth to seize Xian's position.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「本朝傾覆，吳為脣齒，不恤我難，而邀其利，吾寧當為降虜乎！

translations.literal: Xian said: "Our dynasty has overturned; Wu is lip and teeth with us; they do not pity our calamity but seek profit—how could I consent to become a surrendered captive!"
translations.idiomatic: “Our court has fallen,” Xian said. “Wu should be our ally; instead of pitying our plight they mean to profit from it—do they think I will simply surrender?”

sentences.zh: 」乃歸順。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: So he pledged allegiance to Jin.

sentences.zh: 於是繕甲完聚，厲以節義，士皆用命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired armor and completed gathering stores; he encouraged them with integrity and righteousness; the soldiers all obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired arms, gathered supplies, and rallied his men with appeals to duty; every soldier obeyed.

sentences.zh: 及鐘會、鄧艾死，百城無主，吳又使步協西征，憲大破其軍。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai died, the hundred cities had no master; Wu again sent Bu Xie on a western campaign, and Xian greatly defeated his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhong Hui and Deng Ai were gone and no one held the region, Wu sent Bu Xie west; Xian smashed his army.

sentences.zh: 孫休怒，又遣陸抗助協。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu was angry and again sent Lu Kang to aid Bu Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was furious and sent Lu Kang to reinforce Bu Xie.

sentences.zh: 憲距守經年，救援不至，城中疾疫太半。

translations.literal: Xian resisted and defended for a full year; relief did not arrive; more than half in the city suffered plague.
translations.idiomatic: Xian held out for a year without reinforcements while plague carried off more than half the garrison.

sentences.zh: 或勸南出牂柯，北奔上庸，可以保全。

translations.literal: Some urged going south out through Zangke or fleeing north to Shangyong, so as to preserve themselves intact.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged retreat south through Zangke or north toward Shangyong to save what they could.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「夫為人主，百姓所仰，既不能存，急而棄之，君子不為也。

translations.literal: Xian said: "One who is lord for the people is what the hundred clans rely on; since one cannot preserve them, to abandon them in urgency—a gentleman does not do this."
translations.idiomatic: “A commander is what the people depend on,” Xian said. “If you cannot save them, running off at the first panic is not what a gentleman does.”

sentences.zh: 畢命於此矣。

translations.literal: I shall exhaust my life here.
translations.idiomatic: I will die where I stand.

sentences.zh: 」會荊州刺史胡烈等救之，抗退。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jingzhou Inspector Hu Lie and others relieved him; Lu Kang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Then Hu Lie, Inspector of Jingzhou, arrived with relief and Lu Kang pulled back.

sentences.zh: 加陵江將軍、監巴東軍事、使持節，領武陵太守。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Splashes the River, supervised Badong military affairs, Bearer of the Credentials, and concurrent Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Splashes the River, given supervisory command in Badong with credentials, and named Administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 泰始初入朝，詔曰：「憲忠烈果毅，有才策器幹，可給鼓吹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he entered court; an edict said: "Xian is loyal, fierce, resolute, and daring; he has talent, stratagem, and capability; grant him drum and flute bands."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era he came to court; the emperor decreed that Xian had shown loyalty, courage, and resolve and possessed real ability—he was awarded an honorary band.

sentences.zh: 」又賜山玄玉佩劍。

translations.literal: Also there was granted a sword with mountain-pattern dark jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given a sword mounted with dark mountain-pattern jade.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈使持節、安南將軍、武陵太守，追封西鄂侯，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously bestowed Bearer of Credentials, General Who Pacifies the South, Administrator of Wuling; posthumously enfeoffed Marquis of Xi'e; posthumous name Lie ("Ardent").
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was honored posthumously as Bearer of Credentials, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Wuling, enfeoffed posthumously as Marquis of Xi'e, with the posthumous epithet Lie.

sentences.zh: 初，憲侍宴華林園，詔問蜀大臣子弟，後問先輩宜時敘用者，憲薦蜀人常忌、杜軫等，皆西國之良器，武帝並召而任之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xian attended a banquet at Hualin Garden, an edict asked about sons and younger brothers of Shu great ministers, afterward asking elders suitable for timely appointment; Xian recommended Chang Ji, Du Zhen, and others of Shu—they were good vessels of the western state—and Emperor Wu summoned and employed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet in Hualin Garden the emperor asked after the sons of Shu officials and then whom among their elders ought to be employed; Xian recommended Chang Ji, Du Zhen, and others—the best talent Shu had left—and Emperor Wu called them all to office.

sentences.zh: 子襲，曆給事中、陵江將軍，統其父部曲，至廣漢太守。

translations.literal: His son Xi successively served as palace attendant, General Who Splashes the River, commanded his father's military households, and reached Administrator of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi rose through Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Splashes the River, inherited his father's troops, and eventually became Administrator of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 兄子尚。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Luo Shang.

translations.literal: The received edition prints an equals sign here as an editorial or typographical marker.
translations.idiomatic: The source gives only an equals sign as a section marker; there is no wording to translate.

sentences.zh: 兄子尚

translations.literal: Elder brother's son Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang (his nephew).

sentences.zh: =尚字敬之，一名仲。

translations.literal: = Shang's courtesy name was Jingzhi; he also had the name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang, courtesy name Jingzhi, also known as Zhong.

sentences.zh: 父式，牂柯太守。

translations.literal: His father Shi was Administrator of Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Luo Shi, had been Administrator of Zangke.

sentences.zh: 尚少孤，依叔父憲。

translations.literal: Shang was orphaned young and relied on his uncle Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Shang was raised by his uncle Xian.

sentences.zh: 善屬文。

translations.literal: He was good at composing literary essays.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote well.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王戎以尚及劉喬為參軍，並委任之。

translations.literal: Jingzhou Inspector Wang Rong took Shang and Liu Qiao as adjutants and entrusted them alike.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, Inspector of Jingzhou, named both Shang and Liu Qiao military aides and gave them real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 太康末，為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang he became Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taikang era he was appointed Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及趙廞反于蜀，尚表曰：「廞非雄才，必無所成，計日聽其敗耳。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xin rebelled in Shu, Shang memorialized: "Xin is not a heroic talent; he will certainly accomplish nothing; count the days until his defeat."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xin rose in Shu, Shang submitted a memorial: “Xin is no commander of genius—his rebellion will fail; we need only wait him out.”

sentences.zh: 」乃假尚節為平西將軍、益州刺史、西戎校尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shang was lent credentials as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yizhou, and Colonel of the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given provisional credentials as General Who Pacifies the West, Inspector of Yizhou, and Colonel of the Western Rong.

sentences.zh: 性貪，少斷，蜀人言曰：「尚之所愛，非邪則佞，尚之所憎，非忠則正。

translations.literal: By nature he was greedy and lacked decisiveness; the people of Shu said: "Those Shang loves are either wicked or sycophantic; those Shang hates are either loyal or upright."
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and indecisive, he drew a bitter proverb from the Shu people: “Those Shang favors are crooks or flatterers; those he hates are the loyal and the frank.”

sentences.zh: 富擬魯、衛，家成市里；

translations.literal: His wealth rivaled Lu and Wei; his household became a marketplace ward;
translations.idiomatic: His fortune rivaled small kingdoms; his mansion turned into a bazaar;

sentences.zh: 貪如豺狼，無復極已。

translations.literal: greedy as jackals and wolves, without limit.
translations.idiomatic: his greed knew no limit, like wolves run wild.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「蜀賊尚可，羅尚殺我。

translations.literal: Also they said: "The Shu bandits one may still endure; Luo Shang kills us."
translations.idiomatic: Another couplet ran: “Bandits from Shu we might survive—Luo Shang is what destroys us.”

sentences.zh: 平西將軍，反更為禍。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West—on the contrary becomes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: “The ‘General Who Pacifies the West’ only brings worse disaster.”

sentences.zh: 」時李特亦起於蜀，攻蜀，殺趙廞。

translations.literal: At the time Li Te also rose in Shu, attacked Shu, and killed Zhao Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Te had risen in Shu, struck at the governor, and killed Zhao Xin.

sentences.zh: 又攻尚于成都，尚退保江陽，初，尚乞師方岳，荊州刺史宗岱率建平太守孫阜救之，次於江州，岱、阜兵盛，諸為寇所逼者，人有奮志。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Shang at Chengdu; Shang withdrew to defend Jiangyang. Earlier Shang had begged troops from the regional inspectors; Jingzhou Inspector Zong Dai led Jianping Administrator Sun Fu to relieve him and halted at Jiangzhou; Dai and Fu's troops were strong; those pressed by the bandits each had a mind to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te then drove Shang from Chengdu into Jiangyang. Shang had earlier appealed to the provincial authorities; Zong Dai, Inspector of Jingzhou, marched Sun Fu of Jianping to his aid and halted at Jiangzhou. Their forces were strong, and everyone trapped by the rebels took heart.

sentences.zh: 尚乃使兵曹從事任銳偽降，因出密宣告於外，克日俱擊，遂大破之，斬李特，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Shang then had Bingcao Congshi Ren Rui feign surrender and thereby issue secret proclamations outside; on the fixed day they struck together and greatly defeated them, beheaded Li Te, and sent the head to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shang sent his aide Ren Rui to pretend defection, slip word to allies outside, and coordinate a timed assault; they shattered Li Te's host, beheaded Li Te, and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 特子雄僭號，都於郫城。

translations.literal: Li Te's son Xiong assumed illegitimate title and made his capital at Pi city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te's son Li Xiong declared himself ruler and set his capital at Pi.

sentences.zh: 尚遣將軍隗伯攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Shang sent General Wei Bo to attack him; he did not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Shang sent General Wei Bo against him but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 俄而尚卒，雄遂據有蜀土。

translations.literal: Soon Shang died; Xiong then occupied Shu territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shang died soon after, and Li Xiong took control of Shu.

sentences.zh: 滕修

translations.literal: Teng Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu.

sentences.zh: 滕修，字顯先，南陽西鄂人也。

translations.literal: Teng Xiu, courtesy name Xianxian, was a man of Xi'e in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu, courtesy name Xianxian, came from Xi'e in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 仕吳為將帥，封西鄂侯。

translations.literal: He served Wu as a commander and was enfeoffed Marquis of Xi'e.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded armies for Wu and held the marquisate of Xi'e.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，代熊睦為廣州刺史，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao he replaced Xiong Mu as Inspector of Guangzhou and had great awe-inspiring kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao he succeeded Xiong Mu as Inspector of Guangzhou, ruling there with firm authority and genuine benevolence.

sentences.zh: 徵為執金吾。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Bearer of the Mace.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Bearer of the Golden Mace.

sentences.zh: 廣州部曲督郭馬等為亂，皓以修宿有威惠，為嶺表所伏，以為使持節、都督廣州軍事、鎮南將軍、廣州牧以討之。

translations.literal: Guo Ma and others, troop supervisors of Guangzhou, made rebellion; Hao because Xiu long had awe-inspiring kindness and was submitted to south of the ranges, appointed him Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Guangzhou Military Affairs, General Who Guards the South, and Governor of Guangzhou to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When troop captain Guo Ma and others mutinied in Guangzhou, Sun Hao sent Xiu—who had long commanded respect beyond the mountains—as Bearer of Credentials, commander-in-chief in Guangzhou, General Who Guards the South, and Governor of Guangzhou to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 未克而王師伐吳，修率眾赴難。

translations.literal: Before he had overcome, the royal army attacked Wu; Xiu led the multitude to rush to the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could finish, Jin invaded Wu; Xiu marched his men east to defend his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 至巴丘而皓已降，乃縞素流涕而還，與廣州刺史閭豐、蒼梧太守王毅各送印綬，詔以修為安南將軍，廣州牧、持節、都督如故，封武當侯，加鼓吹，委以南方事。

translations.literal: Reaching Baqiu, Hao had already surrendered; thereupon in plain mourning he wept tears and returned; together with Guangzhou Inspector Lu Feng and Cangwu Administrator Wang Yi each sent seals and ribbons; an edict appointed Xiu General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Guangzhou, holding credentials and supervisor as before, enfeoffed Marquis of Wudang, added drum and flute bands, and entrusted him with southern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Baqiu only to learn Sun Hao had surrendered; wearing mourning white he turned back in tears. With Inspector Lu Feng of Guangzhou and Wang Yi of Cangwu he forwarded his seals to Jin. The court confirmed him as General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Guangzhou with full authority, raised him to Marquis of Wudang, awarded him ceremonial bands, and left the south in his hands.

sentences.zh: 修在南積年，為邊夷所附。

translations.literal: Xiu accumulated years in the south and was attached to by border barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He spent many years in the south and won the allegiance of the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 卒，請葬京師，帝嘉其意，賜墓田一頃，諡曰聲。

translations.literal: He died; he requested burial in the capital; the emperor praised his intent and granted one qing of tomb land; posthumous name was Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he asked to be buried near the capital; the emperor approved and granted a hectare of burial ground; his first posthumous title was Sheng.

sentences.zh: 修之子並上表曰：「亡父修羈絏吳壤，為所驅馳；

translations.literal: Xiu's sons Bing memorialized: "Our deceased father Xiu was bound in Wu territory and driven about by them;
translations.idiomatic: His sons Bing submitted a memorial: “Our late father served Wu under constraint—

sentences.zh: 幸逢開通，沐浴至化，得從俘虜握戎馬之要；

translations.literal: fortunately encountering opening through communication, bathing in ultimate transformation, obtaining from captive status to grasp the essentials of arms and horses;
translations.idiomatic: when heaven opened and civilization reached him, even from defeat he rose to military command—

sentences.zh: 未覲聖顏，委南籓之重，實由勳勞少聞天聽故也。

translations.literal: not having gazed on the sage countenance, yet entrusted with the weight of the southern frontier—truly because merit and toil were little heard by Heaven's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: never having met Your Majesty, yet burdened with the southern frontier—only because his deeds seldom reached the throne.”

sentences.zh: 年衰疾篤，屢乞骸骨，未蒙垂哀，奄至薨隕。

translations.literal: Years declining, illness severe, repeatedly begging bones, not receiving downward pity; suddenly reaching death and fall.
translations.idiomatic: Age and illness wore him down; he begged to retire but received no mercy, then suddenly passed away.

sentences.zh: 臣承遺意，輿櫬還都，瞻望雲闕，實懷痛裂。

translations.literal: Your servants inherit his dying intent, convey the coffin back to the capital, gaze upon the cloud palace gate; truly our hearts are torn with pain.
translations.idiomatic: We follow his last wish and bring his coffin to the capital; gazing toward the palace gates we are torn with grief.

sentences.zh: 竊聞博士諡修曰聲，直彰流播，不稱行績，不勝愚情，冒昧聞訴。

translations.literal: We privately hear the Academician posthumously named Xiu Sheng; straightforward manifestation spreads abroad; it does not match conduct and deeds; we cannot overcome foolish feeling and presumptuously hear and appeal.
translations.idiomatic: We hear the Erudites gave him the epithet Sheng—it rings wrong and sells him short; we humbly beg you to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃賜諡曰忠。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon bestowed posthumous name Zhong ("Loyal").
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then changed his posthumous epithet to Zhong, “Loyal.”

sentences.zh: 並子含，初為庾冰輕車長史，討蘇峻有功，封夏陽縣開國侯，邑千六百戶，授平南將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Bing's son Han, initially served as Attendant Clerk on light-chariot staff for Yu Bing; in attacking Su Jun had merit; was enfeoffed founding marquis of Xiayang county, fief 1600 households; appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's son Han began as aide to Yu Bing; he distinguished himself against Su Jun and was made founding marquis of Xiayang with sixteen hundred households, then General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在任積年，甚有威惠，卒諡曰戴。

translations.literal: In office accumulating years, he had great awe-inspiring kindness; at death posthumous name Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Guangzhou for years with authority and kindness and was posthumously titled Dai.

sentences.zh: 含弟子遁，交州刺史。

translations.literal: Han elder brother's son Dun, Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han had a nephew, Dun, who became Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 修曾孫恬之，龍驤將軍、魏郡太守，戍黎陽，為翟遼所執，死之。

translations.literal: Xiu's great-grandson Tianzhi, General Soaring Dragon, Administrator of Wei Commandery, garrisoned Liyang; was seized by Zhai Liao and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's great-grandson Tianzhi served as General Soaring Dragon and Administrator of Wei Commandery; holding Liyang he was captured by Zhai Liao and killed.

sentences.zh: 馬隆

translations.literal: Ma Long.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long.

sentences.zh: 馬隆，字孝興，東平平陸人。

translations.literal: Ma Long, courtesy name Xiaoxing, was a man of Pinglu in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long, courtesy name Xiaoxing, came from Pinglu in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 少而智勇，好立名節。

translations.literal: From youth intelligent and brave, fond of establishing reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he was clever and courageous and cared deeply for honor.

sentences.zh: 魏兗州刺史令狐愚坐事伏誅，舉州無敢收者。

translations.literal: Wei Yanzhou Inspector Linghu Yu sat affair executed by law; the whole prefecture had none who dared collect him.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Yu, Inspector of Yanzhou, was executed for conspiracy, no one in the province dared bury him.

sentences.zh: 隆以武吏托稱愚客，以私財殯葬，服喪三年，列植松柏，禮畢乃還，一州以為美談。

translations.literal: Long as military clerk falsely claimed to be Yu's guest; used private wealth to bury; observed mourning three years; planted pines and cypresses in rows; when rites finished then returned—one prefecture took it as fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long, a minor officer, claimed to be Linghu's retainer and buried him at his own expense, mourning three years and planting pines on the grave—throughout Yanzhou people praised the deed.

sentences.zh: 署武猛從事。

translations.literal: Was appointed Martial Ferocity Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was named aide for martial affairs.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，將興伐吳之役，下詔曰：「吳會未平，宜得猛士以濟武功。

translations.literal: In Taishi, about to raise the campaign to attack Wu, an edict descended: "Wu and Kuaiji are not yet pacified; it is fitting to obtain fierce warriors to aid military merit."
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Taishi, as Jin prepared to conquer Wu, an edict ran: “The southeast is still unruly—we need bold fighters for the campaign.”

sentences.zh: 雖舊有薦舉之法，未足以盡殊才。

translations.literal: Although there are old recommendation methods, they are not sufficient to exhaust unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: The usual recruitment channels miss extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 其普告州郡，有壯勇秀異才力傑出者，皆以名聞，將簡其尤異，擢而用之。

translations.literal: Generally proclaim to provinces and commanderies: whoever has stalwart bravery, outstanding excellence, talent and strength transcendent—each report by name; will select their utmost unusual and elevate and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Let every province recommend anyone of unusual courage or strength; we will pick the best and promote them.

sentences.zh: 苟有其人，勿限所取。

translations.literal: If indeed there are such persons, do not limit what is taken.
translations.idiomatic: If such men exist, send them forward without restriction.

sentences.zh: 」兗州舉隆才堪良將。

translations.literal: Yanzhou recommended Long's talent sufficient for good general.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou nominated Ma Long as qualified to command.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司馬督。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted Sima Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Sima supervisor.

sentences.zh: 初，涼州刺史楊欣失羌戎之和，隆陳其必敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liangzhou Inspector Yang Xin lost harmony with Qiang and Rong; Long stated he would certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Long warned that Yang Xin, Inspector of Liangzhou, had alienated the Qiang and would surely fall.

sentences.zh: 俄而欣為虜所沒，河西斷絕，帝每有西顧之憂，臨朝而歎曰：「誰能為我討此虜通涼州者乎？

translations.literal: Soon Xin was drowned by the barbarians; Hexi was cut off; the emperor often had western-looking worry; attending court sighed: "Who can for me strike these barbarians and open Liangzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin was soon overrun and the Hexi corridor closed; at audiences the emperor kept sighing, “Who will reopen the road to Liangzhou?”

sentences.zh: 」朝臣莫對。

translations.literal: Court ministers none responded.
translations.idiomatic: No minister answered.

sentences.zh: 隆進曰：「陛下若能任臣，臣能平之。

translations.literal: Long advanced saying: "If Your Majesty can employ your servant, your servant can pacify it."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long stepped forward: “Give me the mission, Your Majesty, and I will settle it.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「必能滅賊，何為不任，顧卿方略何如耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If indeed able to destroy bandits, why not employ—only look at your stratagem plan how."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “If you can do it, you shall—show me your plan.”

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「陛下若能任臣，當聽臣自任。

translations.literal: Long said: "If Your Majesty can employ your servant, ought to listen to servant self-employ."
translations.idiomatic: Long replied, “Then give me a free hand to raise and lead the army myself.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「云何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How say?"
translations.idiomatic: “How do you mean?”

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「臣請募勇士三千人，無問所從來，率之鼓行而西，稟陛下威德，醜虜何足滅哉！

translations.literal: Long said: "Your servant requests to recruit brave warriors three thousand men; do not ask where they come from; lead them drum-marching west; relying on Your Majesty's awe-inspiring virtue—how are ugly barbarians worth destroying!"
translations.idiomatic: “Let me recruit three thousand fighters—origin no object—and march west at drumbeat under your majesty’s awe; the rebels will not stand.”

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，乃以隆為武威太守。

translations.literal: The emperor permitted it; thereupon appointed Long as Wuwei Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and named him Administrator of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 公卿僉曰：「六軍既眾，州郡兵多，但當用之，不宜橫設賞募以亂常典。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers all said: "The six armies are already numerous; province and commandery troops many—only ought to use them; should not horizontally establish rewards recruitment to disorder constant statutes."
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers protested: “We already have massive armies—use them; ad hoc bounties only disrupt precedent.”

sentences.zh: 隆小將妄說，不可從也。

translations.literal: Long minor general wild speech—cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long is a junior officer talking nonsense.”

sentences.zh: 」帝弗納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 隆募限腰引弩三十六鈞、弓四鈞，立標簡試。

translations.literal: Long recruited limiting waist-draw crossbow thirty-six jun, bow four jun; erected markers to select and test.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited men who could draw a thirty-six-jun crossbow at the waist and a four-jun bow, testing them against posted standards.

sentences.zh: 自旦至中，得三千五百人，隆曰：「足矣。

translations.literal: From dawn to midday obtained three thousand five hundred men; Long said: "Sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: From dawn to noon he signed up thirty-five hundred men. “Enough,” said Ma Long.

sentences.zh: 」因請自至武庫選杖。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested permission to go in person to the armory to select pole arms.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to choose his own staffs from the imperial arsenal.

sentences.zh: 武庫令與隆忿爭，御史中丞奏劾隆，隆曰：「臣當亡命戰場，以報所受，武庫令乃以魏時朽杖見給，不可復用，非陛下使臣滅賊意也。

translations.literal: The director of the armory quarreled bitterly with Long; the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk impeached Long; Long said: "Your servant is bound for the battlefield to repay what he has received; yet the armory director supplied rotten poles left over from Wei—things no longer fit for use—and that cannot be what Your Majesty intends by sending your servant to destroy the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: The armory chief argued with Ma Long and denounced him at court; Long replied: “I owe my life to defeating these rebels, but he handed me rotted Wei-era staves I cannot fight with—that cannot be what Your Majesty meant.”

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，又給其三年軍資。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his plea and supplied another three years of military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and granted three more years of supplies.

sentences.zh: 隆於是西渡溫水。

translations.literal: Long then crossed the Wen River westward.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long crossed the Wen River and marched west.

sentences.zh: 虜樹機能等以眾萬計，或乘險以遏隆前，或設伏以截隆後。

translations.literal: The barbarians Shu Jinen and others fielded tens of thousands of men; some seized defiles to block Long's advance, others laid ambushes to cut him off from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Jinen commanded myriads—some held rugged ground ahead of Ma Long, others ambushed his rear.

sentences.zh: 隆依八陣圖作偏箱車，地廣則鹿角車營，路狹則為木屋施于車上，且戰且前，弓矢所及，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Long modeled winged cart wagons on the Eight Formations diagram: where the terrain was open he formed deer-antler wagon camps; where the road was narrow he mounted wooden fighting towers on the carts. Fighting as he advanced, wherever bowshot reached, men dropped at the twang of the string.
translations.idiomatic: He built fighting carts after the Eight Formations—deer-antler lines on open ground, timber towers on carts in narrows—and rolled forward, shooting down anyone within bow range.

sentences.zh: 奇謀間發，出敵不意。

translations.literal: Surprise stratagems broke out now and then, catching the enemy off guard.
translations.idiomatic: He struck repeatedly from unexpected angles.

sentences.zh: 或夾道累磁石，賊負鐵鎧，行不得前，隆卒悉被犀甲，無所留礙，賊咸以為神。

translations.literal: Sometimes he stacked lodestones along the road; the enemy wore iron armor and could not advance, whereas Long's men all wore rhinoceros-hide armor and passed without hindrance—the foe took them for spirits.
translations.idiomatic: He laid magnets along the trail: the rebels' iron mail locked them in place, while his men in rhino-hide armor walked through untouched—until the enemy thought them demons.

sentences.zh: 轉戰千里，殺傷以千數。

translations.literal: He fought his way a thousand li; those killed or wounded were reckoned in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: His campaign ranged a thousand li and piled enemy casualties by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 自隆之西，音問斷絕，朝廷憂之，或謂已沒。

translations.literal: After Long went west, word ceased entirely; the court worried, and some thought him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ma Long marched west, silence fell—court officials feared he was lost.

sentences.zh: 後隆使夜到，帝撫掌歡笑。

translations.literal: Later Long's messenger arrived by night; the emperor clapped his hands and laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When his courier reached Luoyang by night, the emperor clapped and laughed with relief.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，召群臣謂曰：「若從諸卿言，是無秦、涼也。

translations.literal: At dawn he summoned the ministers and said: "If we had listened to you, there would be no Qinzhou or Liangzhou today."
translations.idiomatic: Next morning he told his ministers: “Had I listened to you, Qin and Liang would be gone.”

sentences.zh: 」乃詔曰：「隆以偏師寡眾，奮不顧難，冒險能濟。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict declared: "Long led a small detached force, fought recklessly despite hardship, and survived deadly terrain to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Ma Long for winning with a scratch force against overwhelming odds.

sentences.zh: 其假節、宣威將軍，加赤幢、曲蓋、鼓吹。

translations.literal: Grant him lent credentials as General Who Spreads Might, plus crimson banner, curved canopy, and drum-and-flute bands.
translations.idiomatic: He received acting credentials as General Who Spreads Might, with crimson staff, curved canopy, and full honor guard.

sentences.zh: 」隆到武威，虜大人猝跋韓、且萬能等率萬餘落歸降，前後誅殺及降附者以萬計。

translations.literal: When Long reached Wuwei, barbarian great men such as Tufa Han and Qiewanneng led more than ten thousand tribes to submit; those killed or brought over in submission before and after numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuwei, chieftains Tufa Han and Qiewanneng brought ten thousand camps to surrender; kills and defections soon topped ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 又率善戎沒骨能等與樹機能大戰，斬之，涼州遂平。

translations.literal: He next led allied loyal Rong chieftains such as Moguneng to fight a great battle with Shu Jinen, slew him, and Liangzhou was finally pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With allies such as Moguneng he crushed Shu Jinen in battle and killed him, ending the Liangzhou crisis.

sentences.zh: 朝議將加隆將士勳賞，有司奏隆將士皆先加顯爵，不應更授，衛將軍楊珧駁曰：「前精募將士，少加爵命者，此適所以為誘引。

translations.literal: The court debated granting Long's officers merit rewards; the ministry reported that Long's soldiers had already received high titles and should not get more—General Yang Yao objected: "The slight promotions given earlier to crack troops were only bait to draw recruits."
translations.idiomatic: Officials balked at new honors because Ma Long's men already held titles; Yang Yao argued those earlier ranks had merely been recruiting incentives.

sentences.zh: 今隆全軍獨克，西土獲安，不得便以前授塞此後功，宜皆聽許，以明要信。

translations.literal: "Now Long's entire army has conquered by itself and the west is secure—we must not let earlier appointments shut out this later achievement; every recommendation ought to be granted to make clear our good faith."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao argued that Ma Long's fresh triumph deserved full rewards without hiding behind old titles.

sentences.zh: 」乃從珧議，賜爵加秩各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor followed Yao's advice; titles and stipends were increased by graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and distributed promotions and pay raises accordingly.

sentences.zh: 太康初，朝廷以西平荒毀，宜時興復，以隆為平虜護軍、西平太守，將所領精兵，又給牙門一軍，屯據西平。

translations.literal: Early in Taikang the court held that Xiping lay in ruins and must be rebuilt at once; Long was named Protector Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Administrator of Xiping, given crack troops from his command plus one Yamen army to garrison Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taikang he was sent to rebuild shattered Xiping as Protector Who Pacifies the Barbarians and its administrator, with elite troops and an extra yamen corps.

sentences.zh: 時南虜成奚每為邊患，隆至，帥軍討之。

translations.literal: Whenever the southern tribesman Cheng Xi raided the frontier, Long arrived and led an expedition against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Xi harassed the border, Ma Long marched out and attacked.

sentences.zh: 虜據險距守，隆令軍士皆負農器，將若田者。

translations.literal: The tribesmen held strong positions; Long ordered every soldier to carry farm tools as if going out to till fields.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy dug in on rough ground, so Ma Long had his men sling hoes and rakes like farmers.

sentences.zh: 虜以隆無征討意，禦眾稍怠。

translations.literal: Thinking Long had no intention to attack, they relaxed their guard.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes assumed he would not fight and slackened their watch.

sentences.zh: 隆因其無備，進兵擊破之。

translations.literal: Long exploited their unreadiness and attacked, routing them.
translations.idiomatic: He struck while they were unprepared and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 畢隆之政，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: For the rest of Long's tenure they did not dare raid again.
translations.idiomatic: They never raided again while Ma Long held command.

sentences.zh: 太熙初，封奉高縣侯，加授東羌校尉。

translations.literal: Early in Taixi he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fenggao county and additionally appointed Colonel of the Eastern Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixi he became Marquis of Fenggao and Colonel of the Eastern Qiang.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，威信震於隴右。

translations.literal: For more than ten years his prestige shook Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: More than a decade on the Longyou frontier made his name feared and respected.

sentences.zh: 時略陽太守馮翊嚴舒與楊駿通親，蜜圖代隆，毀隆年老謬耄，不宜服戎，於是征隆，以舒代鎮。

translations.literal: At the time the Administrator of Lüeyang, Yan Shu of Pingyi—who was kin to Yang Jun—schemed secretly to replace Long, slandering Long as aged and senile and unfit for military duty; the court recalled Long and installed Shu in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shu of Lüeyang, tied by marriage to Yang Jun, smeared Ma Long as senile and maneuvered him out of office.

sentences.zh: 氏、羌聚結，百姓驚懼。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang bands rallied together and the common people panicked.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Qiang bands rose in alarm across the region.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐關隴復擾，乃免舒，遣隆復職，竟卒於官。

translations.literal: Fearing renewed turmoil in Guanzhong and Longyou, the court dismissed Shu and sent Long back to his post; he eventually died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court reversed itself, removed Yan Shu, restored Ma Long, and Ma Long died still serving.

sentences.zh: 子咸嗣，亦驍勇。

translations.literal: His son Xian inherited the title; he too was fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Xian inherited the marquisate and proved equally fierce.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎攻長沙王乂，以咸為鷹揚將軍，率兵屯河橋中渚，為乂將王瑚所敗，沒於陣。

translations.literal: When Prince Chengdu of Jin attacked Prince Changsha of Yi, Xian was named General Who Raises the Falcon and led troops garrisoning the mid-channel ford at He Bridge; he was defeated by Yi's general Wang Hu and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: During Sima Ying's strike against Sima Yi, Xian led troops at He Bridge as General Who Raises the Falcon until Wang Hu routed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 胡奮

translations.literal: Hu Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen.

sentences.zh: 胡奮，字玄威，安定臨涇人也，魏車騎將軍陰密侯遵之子也。

translations.literal: Hu Fen, courtesy name Xuanwei, was a man of Linjing in Anding—the son of Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Yinmi, Hu Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen, courtesy name Xuanwei, came from Linjing in Anding; his father was Hu Zun, Wei General of Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 奮性開朗，有籌略，少好武事。

translations.literal: Fen was open and cheerful by nature, possessed stratagem, and from youth loved martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and strategic, drawn to soldiering from his youth.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之伐遼東也，以白衣侍從左右，甚見接待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan campaigned against Liaodong, Fen attended him in plain clothes and was treated with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: During Sima Yi's Liaodong expedition he served at Sima Yi's side as a civilian attendant and won exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 還為校尉，稍遷徐州刺史，封夏陽子。

translations.literal: Afterward he became a colonel and gradually rose to Inspector of Xuzhou, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through colonel's rank to Inspector of Xuzhou and Baron of Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 匈奴中部帥劉猛叛，使驍騎路蕃討之，以奮為監軍、假節，頓軍硜北，為蕃後繼。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu middle commander Liu Meng rebelled, he sent Bold Cavalry Lu Fan against him and appointed Fen as army supervisor with lent credentials, halting north of the Gang rampart as Fan's rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Meng of the Xiongnu rebelled, Lu Fan led the pursuit while Hu Fen supervised with provisional credentials, camping north of the Gang as reserve.

sentences.zh: 擊猛，破之，猛帳下將李恪斬猛而降。

translations.literal: He struck Meng and defeated him; Meng's tent officer Li Ke slew Meng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen broke Liu Meng's army; Meng's officer Li Ke killed Meng and came over.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷征南將軍、假節、都督荊州諸軍事，遷護軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For merit he rose step by step to General Who Conquers the South with lent credentials, supervised military affairs in Jingzhou, advanced to Defender-in-Chief, and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards lifted him to General Who Conquers the South with provincial command over Jingzhou, then Defender-in-Chief and Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 奮家世將門，晚乃好學，有刀筆之用，所在有聲績，居邊特有威惠。

translations.literal: The Fen family were generations of generals; only late in life did Fen love learning—he could wield brush as well as sword—and wherever he served he won reputation; on the frontier he was especially feared yet kind.
translations.idiomatic: Generals by birth, Hu Fen turned to books late but mastered administration; on the borders he balanced awe with generosity.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，武帝怠政事而耽於色，大采擇公卿女以充六宮，奮女選入為貴人。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Taishi Emperor Wu neglected government and indulged lust, drafting ministerial daughters wholesale for the six palaces; Fen's daughter was chosen an imperial lady.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taishi, Sima Yan neglected state affairs for pleasure and packed the harem with high-born girls—among them Hu Fen's daughter.

sentences.zh: 奮唯有一子，為南陽王友，早亡。

translations.literal: Fen had only one son, who served as companion to the Prince of Nanyang and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His sole son, companion to the Prince of Nanyang, had died young.

sentences.zh: 及聞女為貴人，哭曰：「老奴不死，唯有二兒，男入九地之下，女上九天之上。

translations.literal: When he learned his daughter had become an imperial lady, he wept: "This old slave still lives, yet I have only two children—the boy lies beneath the ninefold earth while the girl rises above the ninefold heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Learning she had entered the palace he wept: “I still live, yet my son is underground and my daughter is in the clouds.”

sentences.zh: 」奮既舊臣，兼有椒房之助，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: As an old minister now aided by ties to the inner palace, he enjoyed exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: An elder statesman with harem connections, he grew vastly favored.

sentences.zh: 遷左僕射，加鎮軍大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He advanced to Left Deputy Director and added Grand General Who Garrisons the Army with Senior Officials Who Rank as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Deputy Director, Grand General Who Garrisons the Army, and credential-equal chief-of-staff standing.

sentences.zh: 時楊駿以後父驕傲自得，奮謂駿曰：「卿恃女更益豪邪？

translations.literal: At the time Yang Jun, as the empress's father, was arrogant and pleased with himself; Fen said to Jun: "Do you rely on your daughter and grow ever more overbearing?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun swaggered as father of the empress; Hu Fen asked whether power through a daughter had gone to his head.

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代，與天家婚，未有不滅門者，但早晚事耳。

translations.literal: Surveying former ages, kin who marry the imperial house never escape household extinction—it is only a matter of sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: History shows imperial in-laws always lose their houses—the only question is how soon.

sentences.zh: 觀卿舉措，適所以速禍。

translations.literal: Watching your conduct, you are merely hastening disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen warned that Yang Jun's behavior would only hasten ruin.

sentences.zh: 」駿曰：「卿女不在天家乎？

translations.literal: Jun said: "Is not your daughter also in the imperial house?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun shot back: “Your daughter lives in the palace too.”

sentences.zh: 」奮曰：「我女與卿女作婢耳，何能損益！

translations.literal: Fen said: "My daughter serves only as handmaid to yours—what harm or good can she do!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fen replied: “My girl is little better than your daughter's maid—she hardly steers the realm.”

sentences.zh: 」時人皆為之懼，駿雖銜之，而不能害。

translations.literal: People at the time were all fearful for him; though Jun resented his words, he could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers trembled for Hu Fen, but Yang Jun could not touch him.

sentences.zh: 後卒于官，贈車騎將軍，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He later died in office and was posthumously honored General of Chariots and Cavalry with the epithet Zhuang ("Vigorous").
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, honored posthumously as General of Chariots and Cavalry with the epithet Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 奮兄弟六人，兄廣，弟烈，並知名。

translations.literal: Fen had six brothers—Guang the elder, Lie the younger—both were celebrated.
translations.idiomatic: Among six brothers, Guang and Lie were both renowned.

sentences.zh: 廣字宣祖，位至散騎常侍、少府。

translations.literal: Guang, courtesy name Xuanzu, rose to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang, courtesy name Xuanzu, reached Cavalier Attendant and Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 廣子喜，字林甫，亦以開濟為稱，仕至涼州刺史、建武將軍、假節、護羌校尉。

translations.literal: Guang's son Xi, courtesy name Linfu, was likewise praised for breadth and judgment; he served to Inspector of Liangzhou, General Who Establishes Might, lent credentials, and Colonel Who Protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's son Xi, courtesy name Linfu, famed for judgment, became Inspector of Liangzhou, General Who Establishes Might, and Colonel Who Protects the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 烈字武玄，為將伐蜀。

translations.literal: Lie, courtesy name Wuxuan, served as general in the Shu campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie, courtesy name Wuxuan, campaigned against Shu as a general.

sentences.zh: 鐘會之反也，烈與諸將皆被閉。

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui rebelled, Lie and the other generals were locked up.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui turned traitor, Hu Lie and fellow officers were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 烈子世元，時年十八，為士卒先，攻殺會，名馳遠近。

translations.literal: Lie's son Shiyuan, eighteen sui at the time, led from the front rank among the soldiers, attacked and slew Hui, and his fame spread far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lie's eighteen-year-old son Shiyuan led the charge that killed Zhong Hui and made his name known everywhere.

sentences.zh: 烈為秦州刺史，及涼州叛，烈屯于萬斛堆，為虜所圍，無援，遇害。

translations.literal: Lie served as Inspector of Qinzhou; when Liangzhou rebelled, Lie encamped at Wanhudui, was surrounded by barbarians without relief, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: As Inspector of Qinzhou, Hu Lie camped at Wanhudui when Liangzhou rose; surrounded without aid, he died.

sentences.zh: 陶璜

translations.literal: Tao Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang.

sentences.zh: 陶璜，字世英，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Huang, courtesy name Shiying, was a man of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang, courtesy name Shiying, came from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 父基，吳交州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ji had been Wu Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao Ji had governed Jiaozhou for Wu.

sentences.zh: 璜仕吳曆顯位。

translations.literal: Huang served Wu and rose through prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed Wu's bureaucracy to high office.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，交阯太守孫諝貪暴，為百姓所患。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao the Administrator of Jiaozhi, Sun Xu, was greedy and cruel and plagued the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao, Jiaozhi's governor Sun Xu ruled with greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 會察戰鄧荀至，擅調孔雀三千頭，遣送秣陵，既苦遠役，咸思為亂。

translations.literal: When the inspector for military levies Deng Xun arrived, he arbitrarily conscripted three thousand peacocks to ship to Moling; the people already worn by distant labor all plotted revolt.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Xun came to levy troops he seized three thousand peacocks for shipment to Moling; exhausted locals plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 郡吏呂興殺諝及荀，以郡內附。

translations.literal: A county clerk, Lu Xing, killed Xu and Xun and brought the commandery over to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: County clerk Lu Xing murdered Sun Xu and Deng Xun and surrendered the territory to Jin.

sentences.zh: 武帝拜興安南將軍、交阯太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu appointed Xing General Who Pacifies the South and Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan named Lu Xing General Who Pacifies the South and Administrator of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 尋為其功曹李統所殺，帝更以建甯爨穀為交阯太守，谷又死，更遣巴西馬融代之。

translations.literal: Soon Xing was killed by his merit-subordinate Li Tong; the court replaced him with Cuan Gu of Jianning as Administrator of Jiaozhi, but Gu also died, then sent Ma Rong of Brazil in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xing soon fell to his aide Li Tong; the court tried Cuan Gu of Jianning, then Ma Rong of Brazil—each replacement died in turn.

sentences.zh: 融病卒，南中監軍霍弋又遣犍為楊稷代融，與將軍毛炅，九真太守董元，牙門孟幹、孟通、李松、王業、爨能等，自蜀出交阯，破吳軍於古城，斬大都督修則、交州刺史劉俊。

translations.literal: Rong died of illness; the southern inspector Huo Yi next sent Yang Ji of Qianwei to replace Rong, together with General Mao Jiong, Administrator of Jiuzhen Dong Yuan, and yamen officers Meng Gan, Meng Tong, Li Song, Wang Ye, Cuan Neng, and others, marching from Shu into Jiaozhi. They defeated Wu troops at Gucheng, beheaded Grand Commander Xiu Ze and Inspector of Jiaozhou Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Rong died, Huo Yi dispatched Yang Ji with Mao Jiong, Dong Yuan, and yamen officers from Shu; they crushed Wu at Gucheng, killing Xiu Ze and Liu Jun.

sentences.zh: 吳遣虞汜為監軍，薛珝為威南將軍、大都督，璜為蒼梧太守，距稷，戰于分水。

translations.literal: Wu sent Yu Si as army supervisor, Xue Xu as General Who Guards the South and grand commander, and Huang as Administrator of Cangwu to oppose Ji, fighting at Fenshui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu countered with Yu Si supervising, Xue Xu commanding, and Tao Huang holding Cangwu—battle joined at Fenshui.

sentences.zh: 璜敗，退保合浦，亡其二將。

translations.literal: Huang was defeated, withdrew to defend Hepu, and lost two of his generals.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang lost, pulled back to Hepu, and sacrificed two generals.

sentences.zh: 珝怒謂璜曰：「若自表討賊，而喪二帥，其責安在？

translations.literal: Xu angrily said to Huang: "You volunteered to attack the bandits yet lost two commanders—where lies the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xu demanded why Tao Huang had volunteered yet lost two leaders.

sentences.zh: 」璜曰：「下官不得行意，諸軍不相順，故致敗耳。

translations.literal: Huang said: "Your subordinate could not have his way; the armies would not cooperate—that is why we lost."
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang blamed disjointed commands—his allies would not follow his orders.

sentences.zh: 」珝怒，欲引軍還。

translations.literal: Xu was furious and intended to march the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Xue Xu prepared to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 璜夜以數百兵襲董元，獲其寶物，船載而歸，珝乃謝之，以璜領交州，為前部督。

translations.literal: Huang by night led several hundred men to raid Dong Yuan, seized his treasures, loaded them on boats, and returned; Xu apologized, placed Huang in charge of Jiaozhou, and named him vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang night-raided Dong Yuan, seized loot, sailed back, placated Xue Xu, and won command of Jiaozhou as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 璜從海道出於不意，徑至交阯，元距之。

translations.literal: Huang exited by sea where no one expected him and went straight to Jiaozhi; Yuan opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: He took the sea route by surprise and struck straight at Jiaozhi against Dong Yuan.

sentences.zh: 諸將將戰，璜疑斷牆內有伏兵，列長戟於甚後。

translations.literal: As the generals were about to fight, Huang suspected ambush inside the broken wall and lined long halberds deep behind his rear.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting an ambush beyond the ruined wall, he planted halberdiers to guard his rear.

sentences.zh: 兵才接，元偽退，璜追之，伏兵果出，長戟逆之，大破元等。

translations.literal: Battle had scarcely joined when Yuan feigned retreat; Huang pursued, ambushers emerged as expected, halberds struck them head-on, and Yuan's force was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuan feigned flight; Tao Huang chased into an ambush but his halberd line reversed the trap and broke Yuan.

sentences.zh: 以前所得寶船上錦物數千匹遺扶嚴賊帥梁奇，奇將萬餘人助璜。

translations.literal: With several thousand bolts of silken goods taken earlier from treasure boats he bribed the rebel chief Liang Qi of Fuyan; Qi brought over ten thousand men to aid Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He used silk seized earlier to buy Liang Qi of Fuyan, who brought ten thousand warriors to his side.

sentences.zh: 元有勇將解系同在城內，璜誘其弟象，使為書與系，又使象乘璜軺車，鼓吹導從而行。

translations.literal: Yuan had a fierce officer Xie Xi inside the city; Huang enticed Xi's younger brother Xiang, had him write to Xi, and sent Xiang riding in Huang's light carriage with drum-and-flute escort through the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yuan's champion Xie Xi stayed in the city; Tao Huang turned Xie's brother Xiang—riding Tao Huang's carriage with full fanfare—to lure Xi.

sentences.zh: 元等曰：「象尚若此，系必去志。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others said: "If even Xiang rides like this, Xi must already intend to desert."
translations.idiomatic: Defenders concluded Xiang's parade meant Xie Xi meant to defect.

sentences.zh: 」乃就殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they executed Xi.
translations.idiomatic: They murdered Xie Xi.

sentences.zh: 珝、璜遂陷交阯。

translations.literal: Xu and Huang then took Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xu and Tao Huang seized Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 吳因用璜為交州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu therefore employed Huang as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu named Tao Huang Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 璜有謀策，周窮好施，能得人心。

translations.literal: Huang had stratagems, exhausted his purse with generosity, and won men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang combined guile, charity, and popularity.

sentences.zh: 滕修數討南賊，不能制，璜曰：「南岸仰吾鹽鐵，斷勿與市，皆壞為田器。

translations.literal: Teng Xiu repeatedly campaigned south against bandits without controlling them; Huang said: "The south shore depends on our salt and iron—cut off trade and force everything into farm tools."
translations.idiomatic: When Teng Xiu failed to pacify southern rebels, Tao Huang urged embargoing salt and iron until they lacked weapons.

sentences.zh: 如此二年，可一戰而滅也。

translations.literal: In this way within two years they can be wiped out in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: Two years of embargo would leave them ripe for one decisive strike.

sentences.zh: 」修從之，果破賊。

translations.literal: Xiu followed him and indeed broke the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu tried it and crushed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 初，霍弋之遣稷、炅等，與之誓曰：「若賊圍城未百日而降者，家屬誅；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huo Yi sent Ji, Jiong, and the others, he swore with them: "If any surrenders before the hundredth day of siege, his household dies;"
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yi had made Ji and Mao Jiong swear: surrender before day one hundred meant execution for kin.

sentences.zh: 若過百日救兵不至，吾受其罪。

translations.literal: if rescue fails after a hundred days, I accept guilt myself."
translations.idiomatic: If relief never arrived after one hundred days, Huo Yi himself would bear blame.

sentences.zh: 」稷等守未百日，糧盡，乞降，璜不許，給其糧使守。

translations.literal: Ji and the others had held less than a hundred days when provisions ran out and they begged to surrender; Huang refused and supplied grain so they could continue defending.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji ran out of food before day one hundred and sued for surrender; Tao Huang fed them instead so the clock could run.

sentences.zh: 諸將並諫，璜曰：「霍弋已死，不能救稷等必矣，可須其日滿，然後受降，使彼得無罪，我受有義，內訓百姓，外懷鄰國，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: All generals remonstrated; Huang said: "Huo Yi is dead and cannot save Ji—wait until the full hundred days, then accept surrender so they incur no guilt while we keep faith, instructing the people within and reassuring neighbors without—is that not fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: His officers protested, but Tao Huang argued Huo Yi was dead—wait the full hundred days so Jin kept honor and Ji's men stayed blameless.

sentences.zh: 」稷等期訖糧盡，救兵不至，乃納之。

translations.literal: When Ji and the others saw their deadline arrive and provisions gone with relief still absent, they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundredth day came with still no rescue and empty granaries, Yang Ji capitulated.

sentences.zh: 修則既為毛炅所殺，則子允隨璜南征，城既降，允求復仇，璜不許。

translations.literal: After Xiu Ze had been killed by Mao Jiong, Ze's son Yun followed Huang south; once the city surrendered Yun sought revenge, but Huang forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Ze's son Yun marched with Tao Huang and demanded vengeance on Mao Jiong after the surrender; Tao Huang refused.

sentences.zh: 炅密謀襲璜，事覺，收炅，呵曰：「晉賊！

translations.literal: Jiong secretly plotted to ambush Huang; the affair leaked; they seized Jiong and shouted: "Jin bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jiong plotted against Tao Huang, was caught, and condemned as a Jin traitor.

sentences.zh: 」炅厲聲曰：「吳狗！

translations.literal: Jiong shouted back: "Wu dog!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jiong roared back: “Wu dog!”

sentences.zh: 何等為賊？

translations.literal: Who here is the bandit?
translations.idiomatic: Who are the real bandits?

sentences.zh: 」允剖其腹，曰：「復能作賊不？

translations.literal: Yun disemboweled him and said: "Can you still be a bandit now?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun cut him open and sneered: “Still feel like rebelling?”

sentences.zh: 」炅猶罵曰：「吾志殺汝孫皓，汝父何死狗也！

translations.literal: Jiong still cursed: "My ambition was to kill your Sun Hao—what kind of dead dog is your father!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jiong kept shouting that he had meant to kill Sun Hao—cursing Yun's father as a worthless cur.

sentences.zh: 」璜既擒稷等，並送之。

translations.literal: Thereupon, once Huang had captured Ji and the others, he sent them all under escort.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Yang Ji and company, Tao Huang shipped them north.

sentences.zh: 稷至合浦，發病死。

translations.literal: When Ji reached Hepu, he fell ill on the road and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji died of illness at Hepu.

sentences.zh: 孟幹、爨能、李松等至建鄴，皓將殺之。

translations.literal: Meng Gan, Cuan Neng, Li Song, and others reached Jianye; Hao was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Gan, Cuan Neng, and Li Song reached the Wu capital, Sun Hao meant to put them to death.

sentences.zh: 或勸皓，幹等忠於所事，宜宥之以勸邊將，皓從其言，將徙之臨海。

translations.literal: Some urged Hao that Gan and the others had been loyal to their duty and should be forgiven to encourage frontier commanders; Hao followed their words and intended to relocate them to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Advisors argued they had served their masters faithfully; Sun Hao spared them and planned to move them to Linhai.

sentences.zh: 幹等志欲北歸，慮東徙轉遠，以吳人愛蜀側竹弩，言能作之，皓留付作部。

translations.literal: Gan and the others wished to return north and feared eastward transfer would take them farther away; because Wu men prized Shu-style bamboo crossbows, they claimed they could craft them, so Hao kept them in the workshop directorate.
translations.idiomatic: They wanted to flee north, claimed they could make Shu crossbows Wu coveted, and Sun Hao assigned them to the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 後幹逃至京都，松、能為皓所殺。

translations.literal: Later Gan escaped to the capital; Song and Neng were executed by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gan later escaped to Luoyang; Sun Hao killed Li Song and Cuan Neng.

sentences.zh: 幹陳伐吳之計，帝乃厚加賞賜，以為日南太守。

translations.literal: Gan presented a plan to conquer Wu; the emperor richly rewarded him and named him Administrator of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gan briefed the court on conquering Wu and was rewarded with the post of Administrator of Rinan.

sentences.zh: 先是，以楊稷為交州刺史，毛炅為交阯太守，印緩未至而敗，即贈稷交州，炅及松能子並關內侯。

translations.literal: Earlier Yang Ji had been appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou and Mao Jiong Administrator of Jiaozhi, but seals had not arrived before defeat; posthumously Ji was honored with Jiaozhou, and Jiong together with Song and Neng's sons each received marquisates within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors caught Yang Ji and Mao Jiong—titles arrived too late, yet Ji kept his inspector rank and Mao Jiong and others' sons won honorary "within-the-passes" marquisates.

sentences.zh: 九真郡功曹李祚保郡內附，璜遣將攻之，不克。

translations.literal: Merit clerk Li Zuo of Jiuzhen commandery held the district for Jin; Huang sent generals against him but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen's merit clerk Li Zuo sided with Jin; Tao Huang attacked him without success.

sentences.zh: 祚舅黎晃隨軍。

translations.literal: Zuo's maternal uncle Li Huang accompanied the army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuo's uncle Li Huang marched with Tao Huang's force.

sentences.zh: 勸祚令降。

translations.literal: Huang urged Zuo to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huang urged his nephew to yield.

sentences.zh: 祚答曰：「舅自吳將，祚自晉臣，唯力是視耳。

translations.literal: Zuo replied: "My uncle is a Wu general; I am a Jin minister—we shall simply strive with all our strength."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuo answered: “You fight for Wu; I serve Jin—we each owe our utmost.”

sentences.zh: 」逾時乃拔。

translations.literal: Only after a long interval was it finally taken.
translations.idiomatic: The stronghold fell only after a prolonged siege.

sentences.zh: 皓以璜為使持節、都督交州諸軍事、前將軍、交州牧。

translations.literal: Hao appointed Huang Bearer of Credentials, supervisor of all Jiazhou military affairs, Forward General, and Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao named Tao Huang Bearer of Credentials, governor of Jiaozhou, and Forward General.

sentences.zh: 武平、九德、新昌土地阻險，夷獠勁悍，曆世不賓，璜征討，開置三郡，及九真屬國三十餘縣。

translations.literal: Wuping, Jiude, and Xinchang lay rugged and hazardous; Yao and Lao tribes were fierce and through generations had not submitted—Huang campaigned, opened and established three commanderies plus thirty-odd counties under Jiuzhen dependent state.
translations.idiomatic: He carved three new commanderies from stubborn tribal lands in Wuping, Jiude, and Xinchang and annexed thirty counties under Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 征璜為武昌都督，以合浦太守修允代之。

translations.literal: Huang was summoned as supervisor of Wuchang, replaced as Administrator of Hepu by Xiu Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The court transferred Tao Huang to Wuchang command and sent Xiu Yun to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 交土人請留璜以千數，於是遣還。

translations.literal: People of Jiaozhou by the thousands begged to keep Huang; he was therefore sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of southerners petitioned to keep him, so he returned.

sentences.zh: 皓既降晉，手書遣璜息融敕璜歸順。

translations.literal: After Hao surrendered to Jin, he personally wrote instructing Huang's son Rong to order Huang to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After surrendering, Sun Hao wrote Tao Huang through his son Tao Rong urging allegiance to Jin.

sentences.zh: 璜流涕數日，遣使送印綬詣洛陽。

translations.literal: Huang wept for several days, then sent envoys to deliver his seals to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang mourned for days, then forwarded his seals to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝詔復其本職，封宛陵侯，改為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former post, enfeoffed him Marquis of Wanling, and changed his title to General Who Champions the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jin restored his offices, made him Marquis of Wanling, and promoted him to General Who Champions the Army.

sentences.zh: 吳既平，普減州郡兵，璜上言曰：

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified, garrisons were cut empire-wide; Huang memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: With Wu conquered and troop levels slashed, Tao Huang submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 又以「合浦郡土地磽確，無有田農，百姓唯以采珠為業，商賈去來，以珠貿米。

translations.literal: Moreover, "Hepu commandery's soil is barren and stony—there is no wet-field farming; commoners rely solely on pearl diving for a living, while merchants come and go trading pearls for rice.
translations.idiomatic: He noted Hepu's rocky soil forced people to dive for pearls and swap them with merchants for grain.

sentences.zh: 而吳時珠禁甚嚴，慮百姓私散好珠，禁絕來去，人以饑困。

translations.literal: Yet under Wu pearl bans were severe for fear commoners would scatter fine pearls in private; traffic was sealed and people starved.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had banned pearls so harshly that trade stopped and people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 又所調猥多，限每不充。

translations.literal: Moreover levies were excessive and quotas were seldom filled.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy levies still failed to fill quotas.

sentences.zh: 今請上珠三分輸二，次者輸一，粗者蠲除。

translations.literal: Now I ask that top-grade pearls render two-thirds, middling one-third, and coarse grades be remitted entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed taxing top pearls at two-thirds, middling at one-third, and waiving coarse grades.

sentences.zh: 自十月訖二月，非采上珠之時，聽商旅往來如舊」。

translations.literal: From the tenth month through the second, not being season for top-grade harvest, allow merchants to travel as before."
translations.idiomatic: From tenth month to second month—off-season for divers—merchants should move freely.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: The court approved both requests.
translations.idiomatic: The throne adopted his fiscal and travel proposals.

sentences.zh: 在南三十年，威恩著於殊俗。

translations.literal: Thirty years in the south; awe and kindness registered among exotic peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Three decades in the south earned him universal reverence.

sentences.zh: 及卒，舉州號哭，如喪慈親。

translations.literal: When he died, the whole province wailed as if for a loving parent.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the region mourned like bereaved children.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃以員外散騎常侍吾彥代璜。

translations.literal: The court then named Cavalier Attendant Wu Yan to succeed Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent Cavalier Attendant Wu Yan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 彥卒，又以員外散騎常侍顧秘代彥。

translations.literal: After Yan died, Cavalier Attendant Gu Mi replaced Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yan died, Gu Mi took the post.

sentences.zh: 秘卒，州人逼秘子參領州事。

translations.literal: When Mi died, the provincials forced Mi's son Shen to conduct provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gu Mi died locals pressed his son Gu Shen to govern.

sentences.zh: 參尋卒，參弟壽求領州，州人不聽，固求之，遂領州。

translations.literal: Shen soon died; Shen's younger brother Shou demanded the province; the people refused, yet he insisted and seized office.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shen died quickly; Gu Shou demanded the post, ignored popular refusal, and bullied his way in.

sentences.zh: 壽乃殺長史胡肇等，又將殺帳下督梁碩，碩走得免，起兵討壽，禽之，會壽母，令鴆殺之。

translations.literal: Shou then slew Chief Clerk Hu Zhao and others and meant to kill camp supervisor Liang Shuo; Shuo fled and escaped, raised troops to punish Shou, captured him, met Shou's mother, and ordered her to poison him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shou murdered Hu Zhao, chased Liang Shuo, lost him, then Liang Shuo rallied, captured Gu Shou, and forced Gu Shou's mother to poison her son.

sentences.zh: 碩乃迎璜子蒼梧太守威領刺史，在職甚得百姓心，三年卒。

translations.literal: Shuo then welcomed Huang's son Wei, Administrator of Cangwu, to serve as inspector; in office he won the people's hearts and died after three years.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo installed Tao Huang's son Tao Wei as inspector; Tao Wei won loyalty for three years until his death.

sentences.zh: 威弟淑，子綏，後並為交州。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Shu; Shu's son Sui—later generations also held Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Wei had a brother Shu and descendants including Tao Sui who also ruled Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 自基至綏四世，為交州者五人。

translations.literal: From Ji down to Sui four generations produced five men who held Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four generations—Ji to Sui—produced five governors of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 璜弟-{濬}-，吳鎮南大將軍、荊州牧。

translations.literal: Huang's younger brother Jun was Wu General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang's brother Tao Jun commanded Wu forces as General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: -{濬}-弟抗，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Kang was Junior Mentor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun's brother Tao Kang served as junior mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: -{濬}-子湮，字恭之；

translations.literal: Jun's son Yan, courtesy name Gongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Jun's son Tao Yan, courtesy name Gongzhi;

sentences.zh: 湮弟猷，字恭豫，並有名。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother You, courtesy name Gongyu—both had renown.
translations.idiomatic: with Tao You, courtesy name Gongyu—both were celebrated.

sentences.zh: 湮至臨海太守、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yan rose to Administrator of Linhai and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Yan became Administrator of Linhai and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 猷宣城內史，王導右軍長史。

translations.literal: You served as interior administrator of Xuancheng and senior aide on Wang Dao's right army.
translations.idiomatic: Tao You was interior administrator of Xuancheng and chief aide to Wang Dao's right army.

sentences.zh: 湮子馥，於湖令，為韓晃所殺，追贈廬江太守。

translations.literal: Yan's son Fu was magistrate of Yuhu; Han Huang killed him and he was posthumously honored Administrator of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Fu died as magistrate of Yuhu at Han Huang's hands and was honored posthumously as Administrator of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 抗子回，自有傳。

translations.literal: Kang's son Hui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kang's son Tao Hui receives a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 吾彥

translations.literal: Wu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 吾彥，字士則，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Wu Yan, courtesy name Shize, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan, courtesy name Shize, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 出自寒微，有文武才幹。

translations.literal: He came from humble origins yet possessed civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Of humble birth, he combined literary and martial gifts.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，手格猛獸，旅力絕群。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, grappled with fierce beasts bare-handed, and his strength surpassed all peers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, he wrestled beasts and outmatched every man in strength.

sentences.zh: 仕吳為通江吏。

translations.literal: He served Wu as a river-intelligence clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Wu river patrol clerk.

sentences.zh: 時將軍薛珝杖節南征，軍容甚盛，彥觀之，慨然而歎。

translations.literal: When General Xue Xu led his staff south on campaign with imposing array, Yan watched and sighed with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Watching Xue Xu's splendid southern expedition, Wu Yan sighed.

sentences.zh: 有善相者劉劄謂之曰：「以君之相，後當至此，不足慕也。

translations.literal: A skilled physiognomist named Liu Zha said to him: "Judging by your face, you will reach this height later—do not envy it now."
translations.idiomatic: The physiognomist Liu Zha told him he would rise that high someday.

sentences.zh: 」初為小將，給吳大司馬陸抗。

translations.literal: He began as a junior officer assigned to Wu Grand Marshal Lu Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He started as a junior aide under Lu Kang.

sentences.zh: 抗奇其勇略，將拔用之，患眾情不允，乃會諸將，密使人陽狂拔刀跳躍而來，坐上諸將皆懼而走，唯彥不動，舉幾禦之，眾服其勇，乃擢用焉。

translations.literal: Kang marveled at his courage and strategy and wished to promote him but feared the troops would disapprove; he therefore convened the generals and secretly sent a man feigning madness who rushed in waving a blade—every seated general fled in fear except Yan, who lifted a small table to defend himself. All admired his courage and he was promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang staged a fake mad assassin to test his officers—everyone scattered except Wu Yan, who held a table as a shield; Lu Kang then promoted him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷建平太守。

translations.literal: He gradually advanced to Administrator of Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 時王濬將伐吳，造船於蜀，彥覺之，請增兵為備，皓不從，彥乃輒為鐵鎖，橫斷江路。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun prepared to attack Wu and built ships in Shu, Yan detected it and begged for reinforcements to prepare defenses; Hao refused, so Yan on his own forged iron chains to bar the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing Wang Jun's shipbuilding in Shu, Wu Yan asked Sun Hao for reinforcements; refused, he stretched iron chains across the river himself.

sentences.zh: 及師臨境，緣江諸城皆望風降附，或見攻而拔，唯彥堅守，大眾攻之不能克，乃退舍禮之。

translations.literal: When the army reached the border, every riverside city surrendered at sight or fell to assault—only Yan held firm; the main host could not overcome him and withdrew to treat him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin swept the shore, only Wu Yan held out until Jin honored him and stood down.

sentences.zh: 吳亡，彥始歸降，武帝以為金城太守。

translations.literal: After Wu fell Yan finally surrendered; Emperor Wu named him Administrator of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan yielded after the state's fall and became Jin's Administrator of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容問薛瑩曰：「孫皓所以亡國者何也？

translations.literal: The emperor once casually asked Xue Ying: "What caused Sun Hao to lose his state?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan once asked Xue Ying why Sun Hao ruined Wu.

sentences.zh: 」瑩對曰：「歸命侯臣皓之君吳，昵近小人，刑罰妄加，大臣大將無所親信，人人憂恐，各不自安，敗亡之釁，由此而作矣。

translations.literal: Ying replied: "The surrendered marquis your servant Hao ruled Wu by favoring petty men, imposing punishments recklessly, trusting no great ministers or generals—everyone lived in fear and insecurity; the fissure of defeat arose from this."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying blamed petty favorites, cruel justice, and mistrust of generals.

sentences.zh: 」其後帝又問彥，對曰：「吳主英俊，宰輔賢明。

translations.literal: Later the emperor again asked Yan, who answered: "The Wu lord was handsome and talented; his chief ministers were worthy and wise."
translations.idiomatic: Asked the same of Wu Yan, he answered dryly that Sun Hao was brilliant and his ministers wise.

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「君明臣賢，何為亡國？

translations.literal: The emperor laughed: "If lord and ministers were wise, why lose the state?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan laughed: wise ruler and wise ministers—why fall then?

sentences.zh: 」彥曰：「天祿永終，歷數有屬，所以為陛下擒。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Heaven's mandate had run its course; the celestial tally belonged elsewhere—that is why Your Majesty captured him."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan said heaven's mandate had moved—that was why Sima Yan won.

sentences.zh: 此蓋天時，豈人事也！

translations.literal: This stems from heaven's season—how could it be human effort!"
translations.idiomatic: Such shifts were heaven's work, not men's.

sentences.zh: 」張華時在坐，謂彥曰：「君為吳將，積有歲年，蔑爾無聞，竊所惑矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua, seated nearby, said to Yan: "You were a Wu general for years yet remained obscure—that puzzles me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua wondered how a longtime Wu general stayed unknown.

sentences.zh: 」彥厲聲曰：「陛下知我，而卿不聞乎？

translations.literal: Yan sharply said: "The emperor knows me—how could you not have heard?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan shot back: “The emperor knows me—why haven't you?”

sentences.zh: 」帝甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor applauded his wit.

sentences.zh: 轉在敦煌，威恩甚著。

translations.literal: Transferred to Dunhuang, his awe and kindness were conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Dunhuang he ruled with authority and grace.

sentences.zh: 遷雁門太守。

translations.literal: He moved on to Administrator of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 時順陽王暢驕縱，前後內史皆誣之以罪。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Shun of Shunyang was arrogant and unrestrained; successive interior administrators were framed on false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Chang of Shunyang bullied every interior administrator with trumped-up crimes.

sentences.zh: 乃彥為順陽內史，彥清身率下，威刑嚴肅，眾皆畏懼。

translations.literal: When Yan became interior administrator he kept himself pure and led subordinates; awe and punishments were stern and all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan governed honestly and sternly; the prince could not intimidate him.

sentences.zh: 暢不能誣，乃更薦之，冀其去職。

translations.literal: Chang could not frame him and instead recommended him, hoping he would leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to smear him, the prince recommended Wu Yan away.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He advanced to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問彥：「陸喜、陸抗二人誰多也？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Yan: "Between Lu Xi and Lu Kang, who was greater?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan asked whether Lu Xi or Lu Kang was superior.

sentences.zh: 」彥對曰：「道德名望，抗不及喜；

translations.literal: Yan replied: "In moral virtue and reputation Kang does not match Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yan said Lu Xi exceeded Lu Kang in moral stature.

sentences.zh: 立功立事，喜不及抗。」

translations.literal: in merit achieved on campaign Xi does not match Kang."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang surpassed Lu Xi in deeds and battlefield leadership.

sentences.zh: 會交州刺史陶璜卒，以彥為南中都督、交州刺史。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Jiaozhou Tao Huang died, Yan was named Commander of the Southern Interior and Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Tao Huang died Wu Yan became southern commander and Inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 重餉陸機兄弟，機將受之，雲曰：「彥本微賤，為先公所拔，而答詔不善，安可愛之！

translations.literal: He sent rich gifts to Lu Ji and Lu Yun; Ji was about to accept when Yun said: "Yan rose from utter poverty through our late father's favor yet answered an edict poorly—why cherish his gifts!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji nearly accepted Tao Huang's lavish gifts until Lu Yun refused gifts from a man who had slighted their father's memory.

sentences.zh: 」機乃止。

translations.literal: Ji therefore desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji declined.

sentences.zh: 因此每毀之。

translations.literal: Thereafter they continually slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu brothers then kept maligning Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 長沙孝廉尹虞謂機等曰：「自古由賤而興者，乃有帝王，何但公卿。

translations.literal: Filial and Incorrupt nominee Yin Yu of Changsha told Ji and the others: "From antiquity those who rose from lowliness include emperors—not merely ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yu reminded them emperors once rose from nothing.

sentences.zh: 若何元幹、侯孝明、唐儒宗、張義允等，並起自寒役，皆內侍外鎮，人無譏者。

translations.literal: He Yuanqian, Hou Xiaoming, Tang Ruzong, Zhang Yiyun, and others all rose from menial service yet served inside and commanded outside without ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: He listed menials who became great ministers unscathed.
