sentences.zh: 卿以士則答詔小有不善，毀之無已，吾恐南人皆將去卿，卿便獨坐也。

translations.literal: You seize on Shize's slightly imperfect edict reply and slander him endlessly—I fear southerners will all abandon you and you will sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: He warned that mocking Wu Yan's wording would isolate the Lu brothers from southern scholars.

sentences.zh: 」於是機等意始解，毀言漸息矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ji and others' resentment eased and slander gradually ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu brothers relented and the gossip stopped.

sentences.zh: 初，陶璜之死也，九真戍兵作亂，逐其太守，九真賊帥趙祉圍郡城，彥悉討平之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tao Huang died, Jiuzhen garrison troops mutinied, expelled their administrator, and bandit chief Zhao Zhi besieged the commandery city—Yan suppressed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Huang died, Jiuzhen mutinied; Wu Yan crushed Zhao Zhi's siege.

sentences.zh: 在鎮二十餘年，威恩宣著，南州寧靖。

translations.literal: More than twenty years in command—awe and kindness spread and the southern provinces knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years of firm yet generous rule pacified the south.

sentences.zh: 自表求代，徵為大長秋。

translations.literal: He memorialized for a replacement and was summoned as Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: He begged relief and was recalled as Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in that post.

sentences.zh: 張光

translations.literal: Zhang Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang.

sentences.zh: 張光，字景武，江夏鐘武人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guang, courtesy name Jingwu, was a man of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang, courtesy name Jingwu, came from Zhongwu in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，明眉目，美音聲。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, with bright brows and eyes and a fine voice.
translations.idiomatic: Eight chi tall, handsome featured, with a rich voice.

sentences.zh: 少為郡吏，家世有部曲，以牙門將伐吳有功，遷江夏西部都尉，轉北地都尉。

translations.literal: In youth he was a commandery clerk; his family maintained military households; as yamen general he campaigned against Wu with merit, advanced to western Commandant of Jiangxia, then transferred to Commandant of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: A county clerk from a gentry-with-retainers background, he earned promotions fighting Wu—from yamen general to Jiangxia west commandant and Beidi commandant.

sentences.zh: 初，趙王倫為關中都督，氐、羌反叛，太守張損戰沒，郡縣吏士少有全者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince Zhao of Jin was supervisor of Guanzhong, Di and Qiang rebelled; Administrator Zhang Sun fell in battle and few clerks or soldiers in the commanderies survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun governed Guanzhong, Di and Qiang revolted and killed Administrator Zhang Sun.

sentences.zh: 光以百餘人戍馬蘭山北，賊圍之百餘日。

translations.literal: Guang with slightly more than a hundred men garrisoned north of Malan Mountain; bandits surrounded him over a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang held Malan Mountain north with a hundred men for over one hundred days under siege.

sentences.zh: 光撫厲將士，屢出奇兵擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Guang comforted and encouraged officers and men, repeatedly sent surprise troops to strike the bandits, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied his tiny garrison and raided until the besiegers broke.

sentences.zh: 光以兵少路遠，自分敗沒。

translations.literal: Guang thought his troops few and road long and resigned himself to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed he would die far from aid.

sentences.zh: 會梁王肜遣司馬索靖將兵迎光，舉軍悲泣，遂還長安。

translations.literal: Then Prince Liang of Jin dispatched Sima Suo Jing with troops to welcome Guang; the whole army wept and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yong sent Suo Jing to relieve him; his men wept and marched back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 肜表光「處絕圍之地，有耿恭之忠，宜加甄賞，以明獎勸」。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized that Guang "stood in hopeless siege yet showed Geng Gong's loyalty—he should be singled out for reward to clarify encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong cited Zhang Guang's Geng Gong-style loyalty in proposing honors.

sentences.zh: 於是擢授新平太守，加鼓吹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted Administrator of Xinping and granted drum-and-flute bands.
translations.idiomatic: The court raised him to Administrator of Xinping with ceremonial bands.

sentences.zh: 屬雍州刺史劉沈被密詔討河間王顒，光起兵助沈。

translations.literal: When Yongzhou Inspector Liu Shen received secret orders to campaign against Prince Hejian of Jin, Guang raised troops to aid Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shen moved secretly against Prince Sima Yong, Zhang Guang mobilized to support Liu Shen.

sentences.zh: 沈時委任秦州刺史皇甫重，重自以關西大族，心每輕光，謀多不用。

translations.literal: At the time Shen had delegated Qinzhou Inspector Huangfu Zhong; Zhong, counting himself a great clan of Guanxi, always slighted Guang and rarely adopted his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen had left Qinzhou to Huangfu Zhong, who dismissed Zhang Guang as a lesser western family and ignored his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及二州軍潰，為顒所擒，顒謂光曰：「前起兵欲作何策？

translations.literal: When the two provinces' armies collapsed and Shen was captured by Yong, Yong said to Guang: "Earlier when you raised troops, what stratagem did you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: After both armies broke and Liu Shen fell to Sima Yong, Yong asked Zhang Guang what plan he had meant by rising.

sentences.zh: 」光正色答曰：「但劉雍州不用鄙計，故令大王得有今日也。

translations.literal: Guang answered sternly: "Only because Inspector Liu of Yongzhou rejected your servant's plan did Your Highness reach today's position."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang answered coolly that Liu Shen had rejected his advice—hence Sima Yong's success.

sentences.zh: 」顒壯之，引與歡宴彌日，表為右衛司馬。

translations.literal: Yong admired him, led him to a joyous banquet lasting the whole day, and memorialized him as Right Guard Major of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong admired his nerve, feasted him all day, and nominated him Right Guard adjutant.

sentences.zh: 陳敏作亂，除光順陽太守，加陵江將軍，率步騎五千詣荊州討之。

translations.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, Guang was appointed Administrator of Shunyang, added General Who Splashes the River, and led five thousand foot and horse to Jingzhou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min's revolt earned Zhang Guang the Shunyang post and river generalship with five thousand men to march on Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史劉弘雅敬重光，稱為南楚之秀。

translations.literal: Inspector Liu Hong esteemed Guang highly and called him the finest talent of southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong hailed him as southern Chu's brightest star.

sentences.zh: 時江夏太守陶侃與敏大將錢端相距於長岐，將戰，襄陽太守皮初為步軍，使光設伏以待之，武陵太守苗光為水軍，藏舟艦于沔水。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangxia Administrator Tao Kan and Chen Min's general Qian Duan faced each other at Changqi; about to fight, Xiangyang Administrator Pi Chu led infantry while Guang laid ambushes and Wuling Administrator Miao Guang commanded the river force, hiding boats on the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan stalled Qian Duan at Changqi, Pi Chu took infantry, Zhang Guang set ambushes, and Miao Guang hid warships on the Han.

sentences.zh: 皮初等與賊交戰，光發伏兵應之，水陸同奮，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: When Pi Chu and the others clashed with the bandits, Guang released hidden troops to coordinate; land and water struck together and the enemy host was heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang sprung his ambush while Pi Chu attacked; combined arms shattered Chen Min's army.

sentences.zh: 弘表光有殊勳，遷材官將軍，梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized Guang's extraordinary merit; he was promoted General of Specialist Crafts and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong cited his exceptional service and raised him to Specialist Crafts general and Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，秦州人鄧定等二千餘家，饑餓流入漢中，保于成固，漸為抄盜，梁州刺史張殷遣巴西太守張燕討之。

translations.literal: Earlier more than two thousand households of Qinzhou people led by Deng Ding, starving, had drifted into Hanzhong and fortified Chenggu, gradually turning to pillage; Liangzhou Inspector Zhang Yin sent Brazil Administrator Zhang Yan to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin refugees under Deng Ding had seized Chenggu and raided Hanzhong until Zhang Yin sent Zhang Yan against them.

sentences.zh: 定窘急，偽乞降于燕，並饋燕金銀，燕喜，為之緩師。

translations.literal: Ding, pressed tight, feigned surrender to Yan and presented Yan with gold and silver; Yan was pleased and slowed his advance.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ding bribed Zhang Yan into slackening the siege with a fake surrender.

sentences.zh: 定密結李雄，雄遣眾救定，燕退，定遂進逼漢中。

translations.literal: Ding secretly allied with Li Xiong; Xiong sent troops to rescue Ding; Yan withdrew, and Ding then advanced threatening Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Ding called Li Xiong; Zhang Yan retreated; Deng Ding pressed toward Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 太守杜正沖東奔魏興，殷亦棄官而遁。

translations.literal: Administrator Du Zhengchong fled east to Weixing; Yin also abandoned office and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhengchong fled to Weixing and Zhang Yin deserted.

sentences.zh: 光不得赴州，止于魏興，乃結諸郡守共謀進取。

translations.literal: Guang could not reach his province and halted at Weixing; he then allied commandery governors to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to enter Liangzhou, Zhang Guang rallied local governors at Weixing to retake Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 燕唱言曰：「漢中荒敗，迫近大賊，克復之事，當俟英雄。

translations.literal: Yan proclaimed: "Hanzhong lies ruined and borders great bandits—recovery must await heroes."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan insisted ruined Hanzhong could wait for heroes before reconquest.

sentences.zh: 」正沖曰：「張燕受賊金銀，不時進討，阻兵緩寇，致喪漢中，實燕之罪也。

translations.literal: Zhengchong said: "Zhang Yan took the enemy's silver and gold, failed to attack promptly, blocked troops and slowed the bandits, thereby losing Hanzhong—the fault is Yan's."
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhengchong blamed Zhang Yan's bribery and delays for losing Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 」光於是發怒，呵燕令出，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Guang thereupon grew furious, berated Yan to withdraw, executed Yan, and displayed the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang executed Zhang Yan for treason and exposed his corpse.

sentences.zh: 綏撫荒殘，百姓悅服。

translations.literal: He soothed the devastated region and the common people gladly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt trust among the ravaged populace.

sentences.zh: 光於是卻鎮漢中。

translations.literal: Guang then withdrew to garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He reoccupied Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 時逆賊王如餘黨李運、楊武等，自襄陽將三千餘家入漢中，光遣參軍晉邈率眾于黃金距之。

translations.literal: At the time remnant bandits of Wang Ru—Li Yun and Yang Wu—led more than three thousand households from Xiangyang into Hanzhong; Guang sent aide Jin Miao with troops to hold them at Huangjin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru's followers Li Yun and Yang Wu marched three thousand households into Hanzhong; Zhang Guang sent Jin Miao to block Huangjin pass.

sentences.zh: 邈受運重賂，勸光納運。

translations.literal: Miao accepted heavy bribes from Yun and urged Guang to admit Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Miao took Li Yun's bribes and lobbied to let him in.

sentences.zh: 光從邈言，使居成固。

translations.literal: Guang followed Miao's words and let Yun dwell at Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang let Li Yun settle at Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 既而邈以運多珍貨，又欲奪之，復言於光曰：「運之徒屬不事佃農，但營器杖，意在難測，可掩而取之。

translations.literal: Soon Miao, because Yun possessed many treasures, also wished to seize them; he again said to Guang: "Yun's followers do not farm but forge weapons—their intent is unpredictable; we can surprise and seize them."
translations.idiomatic: Greedy Jin Miao then urged a raid on Li Yun's treasure-laden camp.

sentences.zh: 」光又信焉。

translations.literal: Guang again trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang believed him again.

sentences.zh: 遣邈眾討運，不克。

translations.literal: He dispatched Miao's troops to attack Yun without success.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Miao's assault on Li Yun failed.

sentences.zh: 光乞師于氐王楊茂搜，茂搜遣子難敵助之。

translations.literal: Guang begged troops from Di king Yang Maosou; Maosou sent his son Nan Di to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang begged Di king Yang Maosou for help; Yang Nan Di arrived.

sentences.zh: 難敵求貨於光，光不與。

translations.literal: Nan Di demanded bribes from Guang; Guang refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan Di demanded payment; Zhang Guang declined.

sentences.zh: 楊武乃厚賂難敵，謂之曰「流人寶物悉在光處，今伐我，不如伐光。

translations.literal: Yang Wu then bribed Nan Di heavily, saying to him: "The refugees' treasures all lie with Guang—now attack me, better attack Guang."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wu bribed Yang Nan Di to strike Zhang Guang instead of himself.

sentences.zh: 」難敵大喜，聲言助光，內與運同，光弗之知也，遣息援率眾助邈。

translations.literal: Nan Di was greatly pleased; he proclaimed aid to Guang while secretly siding with Yun; Guang did not realize this and sent his son Yuan leading troops to assist Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan Di feigned alliance while backing Li Yun; Zhang Guang unknowingly sent his son Zhang Yuan to help Jin Miao.

sentences.zh: 運與難敵夾攻邈等，援為流矢所中死，賊遂大盛。

translations.literal: Yun and Nan Di jointly attacked Miao and the others; Yuan was struck by a stray arrow and died; the bandits then grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yun and Yang Nan Di crushed Jin Miao; Zhang Yuan fell to a stray shaft and the rebels swelled.

sentences.zh: 光嬰城固守，自夏迄冬，憤激成疾。

translations.literal: Guang defended behind the walls from summer through winter, wrath and grief turning to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang held the walls from summer to winter until rage and grief broke his health.

sentences.zh: 佐吏及百姓咸勸光退據魏興，光按劍曰：「吾受國厚恩，不能翦除寇賊，今得自死，便如登仙，何得退還也！

translations.literal: Staff and commoners alike urged Guang to withdraw to Weixing; Guang grasped his sword and said: "I have received the state's deep grace yet failed to extirpate bandits; now I may die by my own hand—like ascending to immortality—how could I retreat!"
translations.idiomatic: Advisors begged him to fall back to Weixing; sword in hand he swore to die in place rather than retreat.

sentences.zh: 」聲絕而卒，時年五十五。

translations.literal: His voice broke off and he died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died mid-speech at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 百姓悲泣，遠近傷惜之。

translations.literal: The common people wept in grief; far and near mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: People across the region mourned him.

sentences.zh: 有二子炅、邁。

translations.literal: He had two sons Jiong and Mai.
translations.idiomatic: He left sons Zhang Jiong and Zhang Mai.

sentences.zh: 炅少辟太宰掾。

translations.literal: Jiong was young when summoned as clerk to the Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiong briefly served the Grand Chancellor's bureau.

sentences.zh: 邁多才略，有父風。

translations.literal: Mai possessed much stratagem and showed his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mai inherited his father's tactical gifts.

sentences.zh: 州人推邁權領州事，與賊戰沒。

translations.literal: The provincials pushed Mai to act as provisional provincial governor; he died fighting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Locals made Zhang Mai interim governor until he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 別駕範曠及督護王喬奉光妻息，率其遺眾，還據魏興。

translations.literal: Adjutant Fan Kuang and protector Wang Qiao escorted Guang's wife and children, leading his surviving troops back to occupy Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kuang and Wang Qiao shepherded Zhang Guang's family and remnant forces to Weixing.

sentences.zh: 其後義陽太守任愔為梁州，光妻子歸本郡。

translations.literal: Later Yiyang Administrator Ren Yin became Inspector of Liangzhou; Guang's wife and children returned to their home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yin succeeded to Liangzhou and Zhang Guang's kin went home.

sentences.zh: 南平太守應詹白都督王敦，稱「光在梁州能興微繼絕，威振巴漢。

translations.literal: Nanping Administrator Ying Zhan informed supervisor Wang Dun: "Guang in Liangzhou could revive the ruined and finish the fallen; his awe shook Ba and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan told Wang Dun that Zhang Guang had restored lost Hanzhong and awed Ba–Han.

sentences.zh: 值中原傾覆，征鎮失守，外無救助，內闕資儲，以寡敵眾，經年抗禦，厲節不撓，宜應追論顯贈，以慰存亡」。

translations.literal: When the Central Plains collapsed and frontier commands fell, he lacked outside rescue and inner stores; with few opposing many he resisted years—unyielding integrity—he deserves posthumous honors to console living and dead."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial praised Zhang Guang's hopeless defense and urged posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 敦不能從。

translations.literal: Dun could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun refused.

sentences.zh: 趙誘

translations.literal: Zhao You.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You.

sentences.zh: 趙誘，字元孫，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Zhao You, courtesy name Yuansun, was a man of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You, courtesy name Yuansun, came from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 世以將顯。

translations.literal: For generations the family had risen through generalship.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long served as generals.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He became provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 值刺史郗隆被齊王冏檄，使起兵討趙王倫，隆欲承檄舉義，而諸子侄並在洛陽；

translations.literal: When Inspector Xi Long received Prince Qi of Jin's proclamation ordering him to raise troops against Prince Zhao of Jin, Long wished to obey the call to arms, yet sons and nephews were all in Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long was ordered to march against Sima Lun while his kin remained hostage in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 欲坐觀成敗，恐為冏所討，進退有疑，會群吏計議。

translations.literal: wishing to sit and watch success or failure, he feared Prince Qi would punish him—caught between, he convened clerks to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Torn between joining Sima Jiong and staying neutral, he asked his staff.

sentences.zh: 誘說隆曰：「趙王篡逆，海內所病。

translations.literal: You persuaded Long: "Prince Zhao usurped and rebelled—the realm suffers him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You argued Sima Lun's usurpation alienated the empire.

sentences.zh: 今義兵飆起，其敗必矣。

translations.literal: Now righteous armies rise like a whirlwind—his defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Righteous hosts would surely crush him.

sentences.zh: 今為明使君計，莫若自將精兵，徑赴許昌，上策也。

translations.literal: For you, honored envoy, the best plan is to lead crack troops straight to Xuchang yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Best plan: Xi Long should march elite troops to Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 不然，且可留後，遣猛將將兵會盟，亦中策也。

translations.literal: If not, stay behind as rearguard but dispatch a fierce general to join the alliance—that is middling strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Middle plan: hold the province but send a strong general to the coalition.

sentences.zh: 若遣小軍隨形助勝。

translations.literal: Or dispatch a small army to assist whichever side prevails.
translations.idiomatic: Worst: commit a token force to whoever wins.

sentences.zh: 下策耳。

translations.literal: That is the lowest strategy."
translations.idiomatic: That was the weakest option.

sentences.zh: 」隆曰：「我受二帝恩，無所偏助，正欲保州而已。

translations.literal: Long said: "I received grace from two emperors and favor no side—I only wish to protect the province."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long refused to pick sides, claiming duty only to defend the province.

sentences.zh: 」誘與治中留寶、主簿張褒等諫隆：「若無所助，變難將生，州亦不可保也。

translations.literal: You together with administrative aide Liu Bao and chief clerk Zhang Bao remonstrated Long: "If you assist none, calamity will arise—the province cannot be protected either."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You and aides warned neutrality would invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 」隆猶豫不決，遂為其下所害。

translations.literal: Long hesitated undecided and was thereupon killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Long hesitated until his own men murdered him.

sentences.zh: 誘還家，杜門不出。

translations.literal: You returned home and barred his gate, not venturing out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You shut himself indoors.

sentences.zh: 左將軍王敦以為參軍，加廣武將軍，與甘卓、周訪共討華軼，破之。

translations.literal: General of the Left Wang Dun appointed him adjutant, added General Who Extends Might, and with Gan Zhuo and Zhou Fang campaigned against Hua Yi, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named Zhao You adjutant and secondary general; with Gan Zhuo and Zhou Fang he crushed Hua Yi.

sentences.zh: 又擊杜弢於西湘，太興初，復與卓攻弢，滅之。

translations.literal: Again he struck Du Tao in West Xiang; early in Taixing he again joined Zhu attacking Tao and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Du Tao on the western Xiang and later helped wipe Du Tao out.

sentences.zh: 累功賜爵平阿縣侯，代陶侃為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he was granted the county marquisate of Ping'e and replaced Tao Kan as Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Merit brought the Ping'e marquisate and Tao Kan's old Wuchang post.

sentences.zh: 時杜曾迎第五猗於荊州作亂，敦遣誘與襄陽太守朱軌共距之。

translations.literal: When Du Zeng welcomed Di Yi from Jingzhou to rebel, Dun dispatched You together with Xiangyang Administrator Zhu Gui to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng's revolt with Di Yi sent Zhao You and Zhu Gui to intercept.

sentences.zh: 猗既愍帝所遣，加有時望，為荊楚所歸。

translations.literal: Yi had been dispatched by Emperor Min and enjoyed timely reputation—Jing-Chu rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Yi bore Emperor Min's mandate and commanded respect across Jing-Chu.

sentences.zh: 誘等苦戰皆沒，敦甚悼惜之，表贈征虜將軍、秦州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: You and the others fought bitterly and all perished; Dun deeply mourned them and memorialized posthumous honors as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Qinzhou with epithet Jing ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You and Zhu Gui died fighting; Wang Dun mourned them and sought posthumous General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 子龔，與誘俱死。

translations.literal: His son Gong died together with You.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Gong fell beside him.

sentences.zh: 元帝為晉王，下令贈新昌太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was Prince of Jin he ordered posthumous honors as Administrator of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan later honored Zhao Gong as Administrator of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 龔弟胤，字伯舒。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Yin, courtesy name Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gong's brother Zhao Yin, courtesy name Boshi.

sentences.zh: 王敦使周訪擊杜曾，胤請從行。

translations.literal: When Wang Dun sent Zhou Fang to strike Du Zeng, Yin requested to accompany the march.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin rode with Zhou Fang against Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 訪憚曾之強，欲先以胤餌曾，使其眾疲而後擊之。

translations.literal: Fang feared Zeng's strength and wished first to use Yin as bait against Zeng, exhausting his host before striking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang meant to use Zhao Yin as bait to tire Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 胤多梟首級。

translations.literal: Yin took many heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin harvested many enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 王導引為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Wang Dao promoted him Attendant Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao named him secretarial aide.

sentences.zh: 南頓王宗反，胤殺宗。

translations.literal: When Prince Zong of Nandun rebelled, Yin slew Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yin executed rebel Prince Sima Zong of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 於是王導、庾亮並倚仗之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Dao and Yu Liang both relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang both leaned on Zhao Yin.

sentences.zh: 轉冠軍將軍，遷西豫州刺史，卒于官。

translations.literal: He rotated to General Who Champions the Army, advanced to Inspector of West Yuzhou, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Champions the Army and Inspector of West Yuzhou and died serving.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians' appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：忠為令德，貞曰事君，徇國家而竭身，曆夷險而一節。

translations.literal: The historians say: Loyalty is a cardinal virtue; steadfastness serves the lord; dedicating oneself to the state and exhausting body alike; traversing peril and ease with one principle.
translations.idiomatic: The historians praise loyalty through peril and ease.

sentences.zh: 羅憲、滕修，濯纓入仕，指巴東而受脤，出嶺嶠而揚麾。

translations.literal: Luo Xian and Teng Xiu rinsed their caps and entered office; they pointed to Badong to receive credentials and crossed mountain ranges to wave the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xian and Teng Xiu took office and defended Ba–Chu through dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 屬鼎命淪胥，本朝失守，郕巴丘而流涕，集都亭而大臨。

translations.literal: When the dynastic mandate sank away and our court lost hold, they mourned at Baqiu with tears and assembled at the metropolitan pavilion for grand mourning.
translations.idiomatic: They mourned Shu at Baqiu and Yong'an like loyal mourners.

sentences.zh: 古之忠烈，罕輩子茲！

translations.literal: Among ancient stalwart martyrs, few match these!
translations.idiomatic: Few ancient exemplars matched their steadfast grief.

sentences.zh: 孝興之智勇，玄威之武藝，滅醜虜於河西，制凶酋於硜北，審楊欣之必敗，譏楊駿之速禍。

translations.literal: Xiaoxing's wisdom and courage, Xuanwei's martial arts—destroying ugly barbarians west of the river, controlling vicious chieftains north of the Gang—discerning Yang Xin's certain defeat, mocking Yang Jun's hastened disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long and Hu Fen shattered barbarians west of the river; Ma Long foresaw Yang Xin's fall and Hu Fen warned Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 陶璜、吾彥，逸足齊驅，毛炅屈其深謀，陸抗奇其茂略。

translations.literal: Tao Huang and Wu Yan raced like winged steeds; Mao Jiong bent before Huang's deep stratagem; Lu Kang marveled at Yan's splendid planning.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang and Wu Yan rivaled each other; Mao Jiong succumbed to Tao Huang's plots and Lu Kang prized Wu Yan.

sentences.zh: 薪楢之任，清規自遠；

translations.literal: In the duty of gathering fuel for state fires, pure regulation reaches from afar;
translations.idiomatic: Their governance drew pure standards from afar.

sentences.zh: 鼙鼓之臣，厥聲彌劭。

translations.literal: among drum-and-drum frontier ministers, their fame rings ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Their battlefield fame grew brighter still.

sentences.zh: 景武，南楚秀士；

translations.literal: Jingwu was southern Chu's outstanding scholar;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang stood among southern Chu's finest.

sentences.zh: 元孫，累葉將門，赴死喻於登仙。

translations.literal: Yuansun, generations of soldiers at gate, went to death likened to ascending immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You's warrior house faced death as gladly as transcendence.

sentences.zh: 效誠陳於上策，竟而俱斃，貞則斯存。

translations.literal: They offered utmost loyalty through superior counsel yet perished together—steadfast principle endures.
translations.idiomatic: They spoke truth and died—yet integrity survives.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：憲居玉疊，才博流譽。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Xian stood atop Jade Stack—talent broad, fame flowing abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Luo Xian atop Yudie—talent renowned.

sentences.zh: 修赴石門，惠政攸著。

translations.literal: Xiu hurried to Stone Gate—kind governance thereby famed.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Xiu at Shimen—his benign rule remembered.

sentences.zh: 孝興、玄威，操履無違。

translations.literal: Xiaoxing and Xuanwei—conduct without fault;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Long and Hu Fen lived irreproachable lives.

sentences.zh: 愚墳畢禮，楊門致譏。

translations.literal: the foolish tomb rites completed, the Yang clan drew ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet folly at tombs and Yang Jun's clan drew mockery.

sentences.zh: 璜謀超絕，彥材雄傑。

translations.literal: Huang's stratagem supreme; Yan's talents heroic.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Huang towered in strategy; Wu Yan in valor.

sentences.zh: 潛師襲董，觀兵歎薛。

translations.literal: Hidden armies struck Dong; reviewing troops one sighed at Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Stealth against Dong Yuan; Xue Xu reviewed armies with awe.

sentences.zh: 惟趙與張，神略多方。

translations.literal: Only Zhao and Zhang—divine stratagems manifold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You and Zhang Guang wielded versatile genius.

sentences.zh: 作尉北地，立功西湘。

translations.literal: Serving as captain in Beidi, founding merit on West Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Captains of Beidi, glory won on West Xiang.
